conceptTag: Choose a hire under time pressure
readerTitle: You have until Friday to hire. Now what?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (대기업 안의 고객지원팀, 회계 서비스 회사) · 이 유닛의 개념 세 가지 적용
insight: 급한 채용은 하나의 큰 도박처럼 느껴지지만, 되돌릴 수 있는 부분과 없는 부분을 나누고 '충분히 좋은' 기준을 먼저 정하면 작고 다룰 수 있는 결정이 된다.
misconception: 채용은 한 번에 최고의 사람을 골라야 하는 되돌릴 수 없는 결정이다. 시간이 없으면 기준을 낮추거나 무작정 기다리는 수밖에 없다.

sources.text: 이 유닛의 개념 레슨 (THK-05-01 가역/비가역 결정, THK-05-03 사전 부검, THK-05-04 충분히 좋은 선택)
모든 인물과 상황은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 인물, 회사, 일정은 설명용 가상 사례입니다. 실제 통계나 연구 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다.
수습 기간과 계약직 활용은 나라마다 노동법 조건이 다릅니다. 카드에서는 법률 조언 없이 일반적인 선택지로만 다뤘는지 게시 전에 확인하세요.

cards.title: You have until Friday to hire. Now what?
body: Maya leads the customer support team at a large regional distributor. One of her five agents just quit. Peak season starts in four weeks.
HR says the opening closes Friday. After that, the budget freezes until next quarter. She has two finalists, and no time to feel sure.

image.label: A manager at a desk with two candidate folders and a wall calendar circling Friday
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 사무실 책상에 앉은 팀장, 앞에 이력서 폴더 두 개. 뒤 벽 달력에 금요일이 빨간 동그라미로 표시됨. 실제 회사 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Sam is ready now. Priya might be better.
body: Sam is solid, has done support work before and can start in two weeks. Priya interviewed brilliantly, but she needs one more interview round and six weeks' notice at her current job.

options.text: Push HR for an extension and wait for Priya
options.feedback: You chase the best candidate, but you risk losing the budget and starting peak season a person short. The cost of waiting is real even when it's quiet.

options.text: Hire Sam today. Any decent hire beats an empty seat
options.feedback: Speed helps here, but without a clear bar you can't tell whether Sam is good enough or just available.

options.text: Write down what the role must do this season, then see who clears that bar
options.feedback: This sets a 'good enough' standard before comparing people, so the choice isn't decided by the deadline or the best interview.

cards.title: Good enough has to be defined first.
body: Maya's list for the next six months had three must-haves: handle 40 tickets a day, stay calm with upset wholesale buyers, learn the order system fast.
Sam clears all three. Priya might be stronger at coaching and process design, but the role doesn't need those this season.
That's **good enough vs best**. Once the bar is written down, "might be better" stops being a reason to wait.

image.label: A three-item checklist with all boxes ticked next to one candidate
image.brief: 체크리스트 인포그래픽. 항목 세 개("40 tickets a day", "Calm with upset buyers", "Learns systems fast"), 옆에 후보 실루엣 하나와 체크 표시 세 개. 깔끔한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: Split the decision into what you can and can't undo.
body: A hire feels like one huge, permanent bet. It's really several smaller choices.
Some parts are easy to adjust: the first projects, who Sam is paired with, a clear 90-day check-in. Some parts are hard to undo: losing the budget, or starting peak season short-staffed.
Seen this way, the **irreversible** risk is actually in waiting. The hire itself has more room to correct than it first seemed.

cards.title: Maya picks Sam. She has 15 minutes before sending the offer.
body: What's the best use of that time?

options.text: Call one more reference to confirm her gut feeling
options.feedback: It may add comfort, but references rarely surprise you. It checks the decision you made rather than the risks you haven't thought of.

options.text: Imagine it's six months later and the hire failed, then list why
options.feedback: This is a **pre-mortem**. Imagining failure first brings up risks you can still act on before day one.

options.text: Send the offer now. Speed is the whole point
options.feedback: You save 15 minutes, but you skip the cheapest moment to spot a problem.

cards.title: The pre-mortem found one gap.
body: Maya's list of reasons the hire might fail had one clear answer: Sam has never handled angry customers at peak-season volume.
So she changed the plan, not the person. Sam shadows her most senior agent for his first two weeks, and they review his hardest calls together each Friday.
The decision stayed fast. It just got a little safer.

image.label: Two support agents side by side with headsets, one coaching the other
image.brief: 두 명의 상담원이 나란히 앉아 헤드셋을 쓰고 있고, 선배가 화면을 가리키며 설명하는 장면. 부드러운 색감. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: Not every deadline is real, and not every hire is easy to undo.
body: Check the pressure first. A deadline set by a budget cycle may bend if you ask. A deadline set by customers usually won't.
And don't treat a trial period as a safety net for careless choices. Letting someone go is hard on them and on the team. Reversibility lowers the risk of a hire. It doesn't remove it.

cards.title: Now it's an accounting firm.
body: You run a 12-person bookkeeping firm. A large client signs on and starts in three weeks. You need a senior accountant, and no strong permanent candidate has applied yet.

options.text: Hire the best applicant so far as a permanent senior
options.feedback: You fill the seat fast, but you make the hardest-to-undo choice with the weakest information.

options.text: Bring in an experienced contractor for three months while you search properly
options.feedback: This turns an irreversible choice into a reversible one. The contractor only has to be good enough for one client, and you buy time to find the best permanent hire.

options.text: Ask the client to delay the start until you find the right person
options.feedback: It protects your hiring bar, but it spends the client's trust, which can be harder to win back than any hire.

cards.softwareNote: Software teams use the same move: a contract engineer covers a fixed project while the permanent role is filled. The contract is the reversible part, and the permanent hire gets the time it needs.

cards.title: Under time pressure, make the hire smaller before you make it faster.
body: Three ideas did the work here:
list: **Good enough vs best:** write the bar before you compare people
**Reversible vs irreversible:** find which part you can't undo. Sometimes it's the waiting
**Pre-mortem:** imagine the hire failed, then fix what you can before day one
cards.callout: **Try it today:** for your next open role, write the three things it must do in the next six months.
